headline: A calm external backdrop and cheap banks set up into earnings season — but a July 27 rate decision keeps the desk from getting carried away.
summary: Heading into the week of July 13, the mood outside Pakistan is friendly: US stocks are near highs, the fear gauge (VIX) is very low at 15.03, and oil has fallen about 13% over the month, which eases Pakistan's import bill. At home the rupee is steady near 278/USD, inflation is easing (11.1% in June from 11.7%), the IMF program is on track, and SBP reserves jumped nearly $2bn — so the desk's geopolitical risk radar reads 'calm' (score 38). The desk is leaning constructive but measured: the story is cheap, dividend-paying banks setting up as their results season begins (UBL reports July 22), while the central bank's July 27 rate meeting is a real event that could sting rate-sensitive names if it surprises hawkish. Regime is neutral, so the read favours quality names in the sectors macro likes — banks, fertilizer, power — over chasing anything speculative.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: SBP holding rates at 11.5% keeps lending margins fat, valuations are cheap (UBL, HBL, NBP all P/E under 9 with covered dividends), and results season starts this week with UBL on July 22.

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Macro tilt favours it and names like FFC and HUBC-adjacent payers carry solid covered dividends; FFC reports July 29 as the next catalyst.

sectors.name: Power (IPPs)
sectors.why: Defensive cash-generators like HUBC screen cheap (P/E 6.7) with 65% margins and a covered 6.6% yield — attractive when the backdrop is calm but the rate path is uncertain.

sectors.name: Oil & Gas (E&P)
sectors.why: Brent down ~13% on the month is good for the country's import bill but trims earnings momentum for OGDC/PPL/MARI; the sector was the single worst performer last week (-648 index points).

sectors.name: Refiners
sectors.why: The July 11 petrol and diesel price hike (petrol +Rs13.18) is a direct tailwind and refiners were the only gaining sector last week, but margins here are thin and the group has already run hard (NRL, PRL, ATRL).

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Macro flags it despite strong recent momentum (MLCF +22%, DGKC +16% over 20 days) — the energy-price hike raises fuel costs and stretched charts leave little cushion.

sectors.name: Autos
sectors.why: Demand looks soft (HCAR and INDU are down over the last month) and thin margins make them vulnerable to the fuel-driven inflation pulse.

watchlist.angle: The cleanest triple-stack on the board. Its best-proven strategy is the 'Consolidation break' (donch20_pullback_break): 2.18% average edge, 76% hit rate, and 80% out-of-sample — and price is coiled just 2.2% under its 20-day high with strong 20-day momentum (+21.9%). Fundamentals rate 'attractive' (P/E 8.52, 30% net margin, a 6.6% dividend covered by only 56% of profit), and it kicks off bank earnings season with results on July 22.
watchlist.risk: RSI is already warm at 67, so it's extended; a hawkish surprise at the July 27 SBP meeting or a soft earnings print would take the wind out of it fast.

watchlist.angle: A cheap, high-yield bank building momentum (+14.7% over 20 days, above both moving averages). Its proven setup is the 'Consolidation break' (1.06% edge, 63% hit rate), fundamentals are 'attractive' (cheapest-third P/E 5.65, 27% margin, and a striking 16.6% dividend using just 22% of profit — very safe), with results due August 28.
watchlist.risk: Higher beta (1.14) means it swings harder than the market, so any risk-off jolt or a dovish-to-hawkish rate surprise hits it more.

watchlist.angle: A defensive power name that screens cheap and is quietly consolidating (sitting just under its 20-day line, RSI a neutral 51 — room to run). Its proven strategy is the '52-week high breakout' (2.07% edge, 64% hit, 75% out-of-sample), fundamentals are 'attractive' (P/E 6.7, huge 65% net margin, 6.6% covered dividend), and it reports August 28.
watchlist.risk: It's stalled below its 20-day average — if it can't reclaim that level the breakout thesis doesn't trigger, and IPPs carry ongoing circular-debt policy risk.

watchlist.angle: The desk's fertilizer pick sits in a macro-favoured sector with a very strong proven edge: the '52-week high breakout' shows a 3.17% average return, 77.8% hit rate and 71% out-of-sample. Fundamentals are 'mixed' but improving (P/E 9.39, forward P/E 7.02 implies earnings growth, 6.6% yield), and results land July 29 — the nearest hard catalyst after this week's rate meeting.
watchlist.risk: It's currently below its 20-day average and about 3.3% off its high, so the breakout hasn't fired yet; the 82% dividend payout leaves little room if earnings slip.

watchlist.angle: The cheapest large-cap on the desk (P/E 5.28, rated 'attractive') in a favoured-adjacent holding structure. Its proven strategies are oscillator reclaims — 'Stochastic reclaim 50' (2.48% edge, 77% hit) and 'RSI reclaim 50' (1.82% edge, 68% hit) — and with RSI sitting right at the 50 pivot it is exactly at the level those setups watch. Results are due August 27.
watchlist.risk: It pays no dividend, so the whole return rides on price; it's below its 20-day line and momentum is flat, so the reclaim trigger may simply not arrive.

catalysts.event: UBL results — first bank of the season, sets the tone
Nestle, Fauji Foods and Honda Atlas results
SBP monetary policy meeting — first decision of FY27; the week's biggest swing factor for rate-sensitive banks and cyclicals

risks: The July 27 SBP meeting is the key event — after a surprise 100bp hike back in April, a hawkish move would pressure banks and cyclicals despite the calm external tape.
Inflation is still double-digit and just got a fresh push from the July 11 petrol/diesel hike (+Rs13-14/litre), which could keep the central bank cautious.

The Middle East is still a live wire — the July 9 US-Iran flare-up wiped Rs474bn off the market in one session, and a strong US dollar (DXY +1.2% on the month) can drain money out of frontier markets like Pakistan.
